svg.title: Start-up of a Visual Basic Windows Forms application that uses the Application Framework
svg.desc: The compiler-generated Main calls MyApplication.Run. A single-instance check comes first, then OnInitialize raises ApplyApplicationDefaults and shows the splash screen, OnStartup raises Startup, OnRun calls OnCreateMainForm and enters the message loop, and OnShutdown raises Shutdown after the main form closes. UnhandledException, StartupNextInstance and NetworkAvailabilityChanged can be raised while the application runs.
svg.text: Start-up of a Windows Forms application with the Application Framework
left: the steps WindowsFormsApplicationBase.Run performs; right: the Application Event (in ApplicationEvents.vb) raised at that step
Your project (MyType = WindowsForms)
Application Events you can handle
1. MyApplication.Main(Args) (generated by the compiler)
[STAThread]. Calls Application.SetCompatibleTextRenderingDefault, then
MyProject.Application.Run(Args). You do not write this Sub Main;
a second Sub Main in the project gives BC30738.
2. Run: is this the only instance?
IsSingleInstance = False: go straight to the start-up steps below.
IsSingleInstance = True: the first process opens a named pipe; a later
process sends its command line through it and ends.
StartupNextInstance
raised in the FIRST process, with the second
process's e.CommandLine; e.BringToForeground
3. OnInitialize
Raises ApplyApplicationDefaults, then applies Font, HighDpiMode, ColorMode,
installs the WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext, enables visual styles,
and shows the splash screen on its own thread (OnCreateSplashScreen), unless /nosplash.
ApplyApplicationDefaults
e.Font, e.HighDpiMode, e.ColorMode,
e.MinimumSplashScreenDisplayTime
(the only place to set them from code)
4. OnStartup
Starts the network listener (NetworkAvailabilityChanged), then raises Startup.
No form exists yet. If the handler sets e.Cancel = True, the program ends
here and Shutdown is not raised.
Startup
e.CommandLine (the arguments)
e.Cancel = True stops the start-up
5. OnRun
OnCreateMainForm runs and must set MainForm (Application.Designer.vb does it);
if it stays Nothing: NoStartupFormException. Then Application.Run starts the
message loop. The main form's Load event hides the splash screen once its
minimum display time is over.
UnhandledException
an exception escaped a handler on the UI thread
(or one of steps 3 to 5 with no debugger attached)
e.ExitApplication decides whether the app ends
6. The main form closes
ShutdownStyle = AfterMainFormCloses (default) or AfterAllFormsClose.
Application.Run returns; the network listener is disconnected.
NetworkAvailabilityChanged
raised at any time after step 4 when the
network goes up or down (e.IsNetworkAvailable)
7. OnShutdown, then the process exits
Raises Shutdown. Not raised after e.Cancel in Startup, nor after a crash.
Shutdown
after the last form closed, before exit
The default dotnet new winforms -lang VB template has its own Sub Main in Program.vb and sets no MyType, so none of this runs there.
Set MyType to WindowsForms and delete your Sub Main to get it; with WindowsFormsWithCustomSubMain you start the program and call Application.Run yourself.
Order read from the WindowsFormsApplicationBase source in dotnet/winforms; the event names are the Application Events of the Visual Basic Application Model.
